Updated model runs and any Met Office briefing on July 26–27 will provide the clearest near-term signal for resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent sea clouds and high humidity typical of Karachi's July monsoon pattern are moderating daytime highs, keeping maximum temperatures clustered around the long-term July average of 33–34 °C. Recent official outlooks emphasize continued cloudy, humid conditions with limited rainfall through late July, suppressing the stronger heating that would push readings to 36 °C or above. Model consensus and recent station observations show daytime peaks between 32–35 °C, aligning with the market's heaviest probabilities on 33–35 °C outcomes. Persistent onshore flow from the Arabian Sea further caps intensification, while the absence of a heat-dome setup or clear-sky periods in the latest guidance reinforces the narrow 33–35 °C range as the most probable result for July 27. Updated National Meteorological Centre forecasts and any shift in cloud cover over the next 48 hours remain the key variables that could nudge the distribution.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Marcos A. Gelabert Intl Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pa/panama-city/MPMG.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders see the highest temperature in Panama City on July 28 clustering tightly around 31–33°C because short-range ensemble forecasts from global models show modest spread driven by variable afternoon convection and cloud cover typical of Panama’s July wet season. Current steering patterns and sea-surface temperatures near 28–29°C support daytime maxima in this range, while differences in boundary-layer moisture and timing of showers create the narrow gap between the top two outcomes. With resolution based on official meteorological observations, the market-implied odds reflect uncertainty in exactly how much insolation reaches the surface tomorrow rather than any major shift in the large-scale pattern. New model runs and satellite updates over the next 24 hours remain the key variables that could tilt the distribution.
